body.statement: Construct one total test that, using the lexicographically first minimizer in \(\mathcal K_n\), has rejection probability at most \(a_0\) uniformly on \(\mathcal H_0\) for every \(n\), type-II error at most \(b_0\) whenever \(D(P)\ge C r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\), deterministic tuning, and stated arithmetic and memory costs through dense and sparse occupancy regimes. A valid target cost is \(O(|\mathcal K_n|n+\sum_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) arithmetic and \(O(\max_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) memory, with any sharper certified implementation recorded. Next prove \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\) with constants depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\). Only after that equivalence is established, denote their common order by \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}(n;\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), simplify it in every regime including equality-case logarithms, and conclude \(\rho_n^*\asymp r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\). If the two deterministic optimizations do not match, state the remaining upper--lower gap instead of defining a common rate.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: two independently evaluable finite optimizations must first be attained and matched before their common all-regime order is named.
body.gap: CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008, Theorems 3.3--3.4, directly tests an unknown constant-CATE null with sieve asymptotics; SantAnna2021, Theorem 6, tests homogeneous restricted CATE with censored duration outcomes; DaiStern2022 tests equality of additive effects across finitely many prespecified strata; and DaiShenStern2023, Theorems 1--2, gives the observational propensity-reweighted extension for such strata. ChangLeeWhang2015 supplies asymptotic kernel tests for conditional treatment-effect restrictions, while DingFellerMiratrix2016, ChungOlivares2021, and ImaiLi2025 cover sharp unit-effect, distribution-shift, or score-defined group-average nulls in randomized experiments. None supplies uniform finite-sample calibration or the continuous-covariate constant-CATE three-index Hölder minimax radius represented by the two independent optimizations.
body.consumer: The result supplies a detectability benchmark and an omnibus procedure for causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows without certifying any fitted forest.
